rationale: Evidence: every development trial ends off track. Max error sits at about 0.06 m, the off-track limit, in all tracks and seeds, and RMS error is about 0.03 m. Iterations 2 and 4 scored identically (132.0028) even though kd went from 0.4 to 1.0 and kp from 3.0 to 2.8, so the controller gains are not the binding limit at this geometry. The widened 5-sensor span (x = -0.06 to +0.06, 16 mm footprint) cut line-loss events sharply, so sensing coverage is now adequate. The remaining failure is the robot drifting to 0.06 m too early, and the body is the only other lever I haven't tested. Changes: (1) Lower mass from 0.8 to 0.5 kg and shorten the body from 0.18 to 0.14 m (width 0.12 to 0.10 m). Yaw inertia scales with mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, so this cuts it by roughly 60 percent, letting the wheels correct the heading faster. body_width stays above the point where it matters for the off-track limit. (2) Move the sensor row forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07 to give more phase lead before the robot reaches the edge. (3) Keep the sensor span, footprint, kp 3.0, kd 0.4, ki 0 and base_speed 1.3 as in iteration 2, so this race isolates the inertia and lead change. Expected result: lower max error and fewer off-track ends, with progress above the 0.27 to 0.45 range seen so far. Finishing within 3 s still needs a later speed increase. If progress rises but stays short of the finish, the next step is base_speed toward 1.6.
